notes.summary:
How an edit travels on dev. A key press becomes an Action (Keyboard.handle_key_event). CodeEditable wraps it as Perform and calls Editor.Update.update, which runs Perform.go on the zipper. The zipper is a cursor into a Segment: a list of pieces (tiles, grout, whitespace, projectors), and every tile carries an id. Perform.go reads the PREVIOUS statics: insertion, the completion buffer and problem navigation all consult the old info map and error_ids. Main.apply then runs a "calculate" phase after every action, which goes Page -> Editors -> mode (e.g. ScratchMode) -> CellEditor -> CodeWithStatics.Update.calculate. While you type, a 225 ms debounce (StaticsDebounce) holds statics back ("Defer"). When the timer fires it sends RefreshStatics ("Force"). A projector or livelit commit forces statics at once.

When statics does run, CachedStatics.init parses the zipper a second time, apart from the syntax parse. The semantic parse fills in missing pieces of the visible segment (the canonical completion), then turns tiles into an Exp.t whose ids are the tile ids. Statics.mk then runs uexp_to_info_map over the whole program, starting from an empty map. The result is the info map (Id -> Info, last write wins) plus the elaborated program. Dev has no per-subterm reuse in statics, only a whole-program memo. Statics runs synchronously on the main thread. From the info map CachedStatics derives error_ids, warning_ids and probe targets.

The same calculate pass then rebuilds the syntax cache (CachedSyntax: its own parse of the segment, the layout, projector shapes, each fed the info map). It recomputes the completion buffer from the Info at the caret and runs the probe effects. Finally EvalResult projects the info map to EvalInfo (elab_term, co_ctx and probe_targets per expression id) and posts {elaborated program, EvalInfo, previous incremental state} to the eval worker. The worker's results come back as actions, go through update and calculate again, and are drawn by the view.

Everything downstream reads the info map by id:
- the cursor inspector (Indicated.ci_of at the caret's piece)
- error and warning marks (error_ids)
- completion (Info.ctx and ana)
- projectors and livelits (the Info at the projector's id; livelits look up their definition in that Info's ctx)
- probes (ctx and co_ctx through refs_in, ancestors through AutoProbe)
- the worker's reuse check (elab_term and co_ctx per id)

So in statics, whichever analysis writes a node's Info LAST is the one every consumer sees.

What PR #2651 changes, seen from the pipeline. On dev, `module M = def in body` is analyzed as a Let. The Let analyzes def twice itself: a probe whose map is thrown away, then the recorded pass. The ModuleExp case then analyzes def a third time, directly, and that pass overwrites every Info in def's subtree. With the PR the Let's recorded Info survives, and the definition's elaboration is read back from the Info at rep_id(def). So def is analyzed 2 times instead of 3; with #2603 ("a let is analyzed once unless it refers to itself", not yet on dev) it would be 1.

In the common case the surviving Info differs from dev's only in ancestors: the ModuleExp id now appears twice, as it already did for body. But there are two places where the read-back is not equivalent to dev:
- **Function-valued modules.** The Let treats a function definition as possibly recursive. Its Infos then carry a ctx with the module's own name bound, unless the definition uses the name and a FixF results, which is the only case the PR's names_itself guard catches. Completion would then suggest F inside F's own definition, and using it is an error.
- **One-member signatures.** For a module ascribed a one-member signature, def is analyzed against a singleton labeled product. There autolabel_singleton_tuple records one elaboration (the inner one) but returns another (the wrapper). That is why the new evaluator test changes M.x from "the whole unelaborated module" to 1. The PR's premise "add records exactly the elab_term it returns" does not hold on that path.

facts.claim: A Segment is a list of pieces: Tile | Grout | Secondary | Projector. A tile carries an id, a form, a cached sort, its present shards and its child segments. The derived equality ignores the tile id.
Zipper.t = {selection, relatives, caret, refractors}. Refractors hold the manual probes and the ephemeral (auto) probes.
Editor.Model.t = {root sort, state: {zipper, col_target}, syntax: CachedSyntax.t}.
A key becomes an Action.t (e.g. Insert(key)), and CodeEditable wraps it as Update.Perform.
CodeEditable.Update.update calls Editor.Update.update with the model's CURRENT (pre-edit) statics and dynamics. The result is Updated.t with is_edit set from Action.is_edit.
Editor.Update.update clears the completion buffer, records the column target, then runs Perform.go(~statics=old_statics, ~syntax, a, state, ~root).

Perform.go consults the previous info map during the edit: Introduce, the completion buffer, character insertion (Insert.go ~ci), problem navigation over error_ids/warning_ids, and the projector actions (statics.elaborated).
Main.apply runs an update phase, then a calculate phase, on every action. Updated.t has a recalculate flag, but Main does not read it.
Page.calculate runs Editors.Update.calculate, then computes cursor info against the post-calculate editors, then the ExplainThis color highlights.
ScratchMode.calculate takes a StaticsMode from StaticsDebounce.consume, runs CellEditor.Update.calculate with a queue_worker callback, then sends the queued batch with EvalRequest.request.

Statics debounce: 225 ms. An edit gives Defer and (re)arms a timer. When it fires, the timer sets force_on_next and dispatches RefreshStatics, which yields Force. A projector commit (AgentPulse.projector_commit, set by ProjectorPerform SetSyntax) forces statics immediately.

CodeWithStatics.Update.calculate recomputes statics only when the mode is Force, or the probe set changed, or (is_edited and not Defer). Otherwise it keeps the old statics and clears only completion. It then runs Editor.Update.calculate, re-inits statics if autoprobe changed the probes, and refreshes targets.
Statics recompute time is recorded by PerfMetrics.time_statics around CachedStatics.init (the Statics section of the debug sidebar).

CachedStatics.init runs MakeTerm.from_zip_for_sem_with_completion(z, ~root), applies stitch, collects the probe ids from the zipper, and calls init_from_term. That calls Statics.mk, then derives error_ids, warning_ids and targets.
CachedStatics.t = {term, elaborated, info_map, error_ids, warning_ids, completion, targets}.
The semantic parse erases the buffer, zips the zipper, takes the canonical completion of the segment, and parses the completed segment with go_impl.
MakeTerm gives each term the ids of the tiles that make it up (plus adopted inner ids) and registers the term under all of them in TermMap. A term's rep id is the head of that list.

Aside (not this PR): from_zip_for_sem_with_completion takes ~root after z (MakeTerm.re:1997), so Core.Memo.general memoizes only on z and caches a partial application. The conversion appears to run on every call, while the memo still holds up to 1000 zippers. Worth confirming.

Statics.mk memoizes the whole program on (ana, ctx, term, probe_ids), with cache bound 1000. It runs uexp_to_info_map from Id.Map.empty and then copies Info to sibling shard ids. Statics has no per-subterm incrementality on dev.
Statics.Map.t = Id.Map.t(Info.t). add_info is Id.Map.add over a list of ids, so the last write wins. error_ids and warning_ids are folds over the map that keep only representative ids.

Info.t = InfoDrv | InfoExp | InfoPat | InfoTyp | InfoTPat | InfoMod | InfoSig | InfoMPat | Secondary. Info.exp holds user_term, elab_term, ancestors, ctx, ana, elab_syn_ty, marks, co_ctx, probe_targets, cls, message, warnings, ty and the label fields.
Inside uexp_to_info_map, add builds the InfoExp, records it at IdTagged.ids(user_term), and returns the same elab_term it recorded. go passes ancestors_inclusive = [rep_id(uexp)] @ ancestors.

CachedSyntax.mk runs its OWN parse, MakeTerm.go(segment) (memoized on the segment), for terms, term_data and projectors. Projector shapes and refractor rows come from the info map, dynamics and elaborated program, then the layout is measured. calculate chooses between a full mk, refresh_shapes, or selection-only, by physical equality of info_map, dyn_map and elaborated.

Editor.Update.calculate sets the completion buffer from Indicated.ci_for_completion(zipper, info_map), recalculates CachedSyntax, then runs ProbeFocus.editor_effects and AutoProbe, all with statics.info_map.
Cursor inspector: Indicated.ci_of looks up the Info at the indicated piece's id. CodeWithStatics.Model.get_cursor_info builds the Cursor record, and CursorInspector.view renders it from Page.
Error and warning marks are drawn by Arms.Errors.of_ids over statics.error_ids and warning_ids.
Completion: TyDi.set_buffer suggests from the Info at the caret, and variable suggestions iterate Info.ctx_of(ci) filtered for shadowing.

Projectors receive the Info at their own id. When elaborate_syntax is set, they also receive their elaborated subterm, found by id in CachedStatics.elaborated. The livelit projector looks up the livelit definition in that Info's ctx.

EvalResult.calculate projects the info map to EvalInfo, because LivelitCtx closures cannot cross postMessage. It queues {expr: elaborated, eval_info_map, prev} to the worker, or evaluates synchronously when there is no worker (ExplainThis examples). Re-evaluation is gated on the elaborated program, settings and targets changing.
EvalInfo keeps, for every InfoExp id, its elab_term, co_ctx and probe_targets, plus the sample targets.

Worker protocol: a Request.value is {expr, eval_info_map, prev}. WorkerClient.request posts the batch and starts the timeouts. Results come back through callbacks that EvalRequest turns into EvalResult actions (UpdateResult, streaming merges).
The worker's incremental reuse_check at an id requires the previous elab to equal info.elab_term (fast_equal plus lexeme trace), and the reuse map restricted to info.co_ctx to be unchanged.

CellEditor.calculate calculates the editor, then the result (which may queue a worker request). If dynamics changed or a probe focus or cursor is pending, it runs a second editor pass with is_edited=false.

ModuleExp on dev: record MPat info; build expanded = fast_copy(rep_id(uexp), Let(mpat_to_pat(mp), def, body)); analyze it with go(~ana); override cls; then analyze def again directly with go(~ana=def_ana, def, m), which re-records def's whole subtree; then splice that elaboration in with moduleexp_elab and add.

The Let case analyzes def more than once on dev. Every Let runs a recursion probe at 2070 (map discarded). The non-recursive path then records the pass at 2079. The recursive path runs 2091 and 2103 (discarded) and records 2121 in def_ctx, where the binder is in scope. So a non-recursive module definition is analyzed 3 times on dev (2070, 2079, 2762) and 2 with the PR. A function-valued one: 5 on dev, 4 with the PR (5 if it names itself).

is_recursive is structural: a pattern with one variable and a def that is one function of arrow-like type counts as recursive. So `module F = fun x -> ...` takes the recursive path whether or not it mentions F.

requires_fixf = is_rec and (def.co_ctx, body.co_ctx minus the binders, or the pattern's type refs mention a bound var). Only then is the elaboration Let(p, FixF(...), body), and the Let then strips the binders from the co_ctx at fun_id. The Let already reads Info back from the map here.
moduleexp_elab keeps the Let's pattern and body elaboration but substitutes def_elab_direct for the definition. If the expanded elaboration is not a Let, it ignores def_elab_direct.

PR change: names_itself = expanded_elab.term is Let(_, FixF(_), _). If the Info at Exp.rep_id(def) is an InfoExp and names_itself is false, its elab_term becomes def_elab_direct. Otherwise the old direct analysis runs.

autolabel_singleton_tuple records inner_for_source (elab_term from analyzing a fresh-id copy against the field type) at uexp's ids, but returns elaborated_exp: an unelaborated Tuple([TupLabel(l, original_expression)]) carrying uexp's annotation. Here the recorded elab and the returned elab differ.
Every expression analyzed against a singleton labeled product whose synthesized type is not that same singleton goes through autolabel_singleton_tuple.
A one-member signature `{ let x : Int }` desugars to Prod([TupLabel(x, Int)]), a singleton labeled product. mpat_to_pat and the pattern Asc case both desugar the signature this way.

New evaluator test: `module M : { let x : Int } = { let x = 1; let y = 2 } in M.x` evaluates to 1. Its comment says that before the PR, M.x was the whole unelaborated module, which matches dev's direct analysis returning the autolabel wrapper.
New statics test: `module F = fun x -> F(x) in 1` must be inconsistent, because modules are not recursive.

Because expanded carries uexp's rep id (fast_copy), the Let's children get ancestors [M, M, ...outer]. With the PR, def's subtree keeps those, where dev's direct pass wrote [M, ...outer]. The body already had the duplicate on dev. AutoProbe already removes adjacent duplicate ancestors.
Other consumers of Info.ancestors: EvalWorklist (is_inside_function, parent_id_of), ProblemCollection, ProbePerform and StaticsBase climbs, the DebugSidebar.
Pre-existing dead write: the 'Override cls' add_info at uexp's ids is overwritten by the final add, which writes the same ids. That add's cls is already Exp(ModuleExp).
Pre-existing last-write-wins effect: the ModuleExp case records InfoMPat for the module name. The Let's go_pat then records InfoPat at the same id, because mpat_to_pat fast_copies MPat.rep_id.

Tuple-valued definitions: before analyzing, the Let rearranges a Tuple def to match a Prod pattern type, keeping the rep id. align_exp_if_needed is applied only after the recorded pass. So the read-back elab is of the rearranged tuple, not yet aligned.
Other places where statics reads its own map in mid-analysis: module_actual_type reads pattern Infos for export types, and reclassify_expanded_module_items rewrites cls.

#2603 (a let is analyzed once unless it refers to itself) is not on origin/dev; its commit is 4eec302a50. For function-shaped defs it keeps the probe, which is analyzed in p_syn.ctx, where the binder is in scope. is_rec and requires_fixf are unchanged.

representations.consumed_by: MakeTerm (both parses), Measured layout, CanonicalCompletion, Printer

representations.what: Cursor into the segment: selection, relatives (siblings and ancestors), caret, and refractors (manual and ephemeral probes, sample focus).
representations.produced_by: Perform.go (Editor.re:173-174), ProbeFocus/AutoProbe in Editor.Update.calculate
representations.consumed_by: CachedStatics.init (probe ids, semantic parse), CachedSyntax.calculate, Indicated.ci_of, the view

diagram_ideas: EDIT ROUND TRIP, two swimlanes (MAIN THREAD | EVAL WORKER). Main lane, top to bottom: [Key event] -> 'Keyboard.handle_key_event' -> [Action.t] -> 'CodeEditable.Update.update' -> [Editor.Update.update] -> [Perform.go] (side arrow IN from a [CachedStatics (OLD)] box, labeled 'ci for Insert/Buffer, error_ids for NextProblem') -> [new Zipper] -> 'Updated.t {is_edit}' -> [Main.apply: CALCULATE phase] -> [Page -> Editors -> ScratchMode.calculate] -> [StaticsDebounce.consume] with three exits: 'Defer (typing, 225 ms timer)', 'Normal', 'Force (timer fired / projector commit)'. A dashed arrow from the timer loops back to the top as action 'RefreshStatics'. Normal/Force -> [CodeWithStatics.calculate: needs_refresh?] -> [CachedStatics.init] -> [MakeTerm: canonical completion + go_impl] -> [Exp.t, ids = tile ids] -> [Statics.mk: whole program, empty map] -> [info_map + elaborated] -> [error_ids / warning_ids / targets] -> [Editor.Update.calculate: TyDi buffer, CachedSyntax, probes] -> [EvalResult.calculate: EvalInfo.of_info_map]. Arrow across to the worker lane labeled 'postMessage {elaborated, EvalInfo, prev}' -> [Evaluator + IncrEval.reuse_check] -> arrow back labeled 'UpdateResult / streaming actions' -> re-enters [update] at the top -> [calculate (no statics recompute; CachedSyntax refresh_shapes)] -> [View: code, error arms, CursorInspector].

TWO PARSES, ONE ID SPACE. Left box [Zipper / Segment (tiles carry ids)] with two arrows. Upper arrow 'MakeTerm.go(segment)' -> [Syntax term: TermMap, TermData] -> [Measured layout] -> [view geometry]. Lower arrow 'CanonicalCompletion + go_impl' -> [Semantic Exp.t] -> 'Statics.mk' -> [Id.Map(Info)] and [elaborated Exp.t]. Then -> 'EvalInfo.of_info_map' -> [EvalInfo] -> worker -> [Dynamics.Map (samples by id)]. A dotted line labeled 'same tile id' links one tile in the segment to its TermData row, its Info entry, its EvalInfo entry, its probe sample and its projector. This shows that all consumers meet at the id.

INFO MAP HUB. Center box [Statics.Map.t : Id -> Info (last write wins)]. Spokes, each labeled with the Info fields it reads: [Cursor inspector] 'cls, ty, ana, marks, message (Indicated.ci_of)'; [Error/warning arms] 'marks via error_ids'; [Completion / TyDi] 'ctx, ana (TyDiCtx.re:193)'; [Perform.go] 'ci for Insert/Buffer/Introduce; error_ids for problem navigation'; [Projectors & livelits] 'Info at projector id; ctx for livelit lookup; elaborated subterm by id'; [Probes / AutoProbe] 'co_ctx+ctx (refs_in), ancestors'; [Worker / IncrEval] 'elab_term, co_ctx, probe_targets'; [EvalWorklist / ProblemCollection] 'ancestors'. Mark in red the spokes whose fields the PR can change for a module definition's subtree: ancestors (duplicate M id), ctx (module name bound for function-valued modules), and the spliced elab (one-member signature case).

MODULEEXP, DEV vs PR (two side-by-side sequence diagrams over a shared 'info map' column). DEV: [record MPat info] -> [go(expanded Let)] whose inner Let box has 'probe(def) — map discarded' and 'analyze(def) — writes subtree infos A' -> [cls override (dead: overwritten by final add)] -> [go(def) direct — writes subtree infos B, OVERWRITING A] -> [moduleexp_elab(def_elab from B)] -> [add ModuleExp info]. PR: same through the Let -> diamond 'expanded_elab = Let(_, FixF, _)?' with branches: 'no' -> [read info[rep_id(def)].elab_term (A)] -> [moduleexp_elab(A)]; 'yes' -> [go(def) direct (B), as on dev]. Under the map column, show which infos survive (A or B) and the fields that can differ: ancestors [M,M,...] in A vs [M,...] in B; ctx with F bound in A for the recursive path.

ONE-MEMBER SIGNATURE PATH (why M.x changed). Box [def = { let x = 1; let y = 2 }] analyzed against ana = (x = Int) (the desugared signature) -> diamond 'singleton labeled product and syn type not (x = _)' -> [autolabel_singleton_tuple]. Two output arrows: 'RECORDS at rep_id(def): inner_for_source, elab = elaborated module (top id is fresh)' and 'RETURNS: Tuple([x = <UNELABORATED module>])'. The dev arrow takes RETURNS -> 'M.x = whole module'. The PR arrow takes RECORDS -> 'M.x = 1'. Caption: the premise 'add records exactly the elab it returns' fails on this path.

ANALYSIS-COUNT BARS per module binding's definition. Rows: 'non-recursive def (e.g. module block)': dev 3 (Let probe 2070, Let pass 2079, direct 2762), PR 2, PR + #2603 1. 'function-valued def, not self-naming': dev 5 (2070, 2091, 2103, 2121, direct), PR 4. 'function-valued def that names itself': dev 5, PR 5 (fallback). Footnote: each bar is a full walk of the definition, on the main thread, after every debounced edit.
review_points: Common case is safe. For a definition that is not a function and does not hit the singleton-labeled-tuple path (the usual `module M = { ... } in ...`), the Let's recorded Info matches what dev's direct pass wrote: same ctx, effectively the same ana, same elab. Only ancestors differ: the ModuleExp id now appears twice ([M, M, ...]), because the expanded Let carries M's rep id (Statics.re:270, 2737-2742). The body already had this on dev, and AutoProbe already removes adjacent duplicates (AutoProbePerform.re:81-93). Worth a glance in the debug sidebar's ancestors field; no consumer appears to break.

Function-valued modules change what editor features see. `module F = fun x -> ? in ...` is structurally 'recursive' (Statics.re:2024-2039), so the Let records def's subtree with def_ctx, where F is bound (2090-2122). The FixF guard catches only the case where def actually USES F. So with the PR, the hole's Info.ctx contains F: completion (TyDiCtx.re:193) and the context inspector will offer F inside its own definition, and accepting it turns into the unbound-name error. On dev the direct pass overwrote these Infos with the outer ctx. Suggested fix: fall back whenever the recorded Info at rep_id(def) has the module's own binder in its ctx (or the ctx is not the outer one). A cleaner follow-up is a non-recursive flag on the Let expansion, so modules never take the recursive path. Add a test that checks the hole's ctx.

The PR's premise is false on one path, and the new evaluator test depends on that path. autolabel_singleton_tuple records inner_for_source at uexp's ids but returns a different, unelaborated wrapper (Statics.re:356-358). A module under a one-member signature is analyzed against a singleton labeled product (Typ.re:615-646), so it takes this path. That is why M.x changes from 'the whole unelaborated module' to 1 (Test_Evaluator_Modules.re:86-96 at 29c08fd8fa). This is a semantic change, an improvement but not a pure refactor. The PR description and the code comment ('add records exactly the elab_term it returns', Statics.re:2757-2763 at 29c08fd8fa) should say so.

In that same case the read-back elaboration's top node has a FRESH id (Statics.re:312, original_expression = Exp.fresh(term)), so the elaborated program has no node at rep_id(def). A probe placed on such a module definition may show no samples, and IncrEval cannot reuse at that id (EvalInfo.is_program_node). This only happens in an already-erroneous program; worth one check in the browser.

names_itself inspects only the top of expanded_elab (Statics.re:2770-2774 at 29c08fd8fa). If the ModuleExp itself sits where a singleton labeled product is expected, the outer autolabel wrapper makes expanded_elab a Tuple. A self-naming definition would then keep the recursive analysis's Infos and lose the unbound-name mark. It is an edge case, but it shows the guard keys on the shape of the elaboration rather than on the fact that matters: was def analyzed with its own name in scope?

Statics is now using the info map as a side channel: it writes a node's Info and later reads it back in the same pass. That joins existing cases (FixF co_ctx rewrite at Statics.re:2216-2228; ModuleHelpers.module_actual_type at ModuleHelpers.re:413-439). Correctness depends on which write comes last (StaticsBase.re:10-11). Consider a debug-only assertion that the read-back elab equals the direct elab (Exp.fast_equal) outside the known autolabel case, so drift shows up in tests.

Interaction with #2603 (a let is analyzed once unless it refers to itself; not on dev; commit 4eec302a50). For function-shaped definitions that do not mention their binders, #2603 keeps the probe pass, which runs in the pattern's ctx. So point 2 (the module name visible in ctx) would hold for those as well. requires_fixf is unchanged by #2603, so the FixF guard still works. The two touch adjacent code: rebase one on the other and rerun Test_Statics_Modules and Test_Evaluator_Modules.

Why the saving matters in the pipeline. Statics runs synchronously on the main thread in the calculate phase. It re-walks the whole program from an empty map on every refresh (Statics.re:4354-4362); the only reuse is a whole-program memo. A refresh happens after the 225 ms typing debounce, or immediately on a livelit or projector commit (CodeWithStatics.re:93-141). Removing one of three walks of every module definition therefore shortens the blocking statics step directly. Measure it with the Statics section timer (PerfMetrics.time_statics, CodeWithStatics.re:188), and state the run count and spread, since one timing run is noise.

Consistency with the worker is preserved. In both the read-back and the fallback branch, the Info at rep_id(def) and the elaboration spliced into the program come from the same pass, so IncrEval's elab_term and co_ctx checks (IncrEval.re:313-345) keep agreeing with the program. The exception is the fresh-id autolabel case above.

Small corners, if relevant: (a) a tuple-valued definition is read back from the Let's rearranged tuple before align_exp_if_needed (Statics.re:2054-2069, 2184-2191), whereas dev used the original tuple; (b) pre-existing, not this PR: the 'Override cls' write (Statics.re:2743-2756) is dead because the final add writes the same ids with cls ModuleExp, and the module name's InfoMPat is overwritten by the Let's InfoPat (Statics.re:2728-2735 vs ModuleHelpers.re:53). Both are candidates for a follow-up cleanup.

notes.summary:
Statics in Hazel on dev is one recursive walk over the user's term. uexp_to_info_map (src/language/statics/Statics.re:191) takes a context (ctx), an expectation (ana) and a term, and threads one map, an Id.Map from term ids to Info.t. Every expression form ends by calling the local add (Statics.re:204-269). add works out the error marks, the inspector message and the fixed type, builds an Info.exp record, writes it at every id of the term, and returns three things: the info, the term's elaboration (elab_term) and the new map. So the walk produces two outputs at once. One is the map: cursor inspector, error list, completion, and the incremental evaluator's per-node cache keys, which come from the InfoExp elab_term and co_ctx (EvalInfo.re:56-73, IncrEval.re:328-334). The other is the returned elaboration of the whole program, which Statics.mk hands to evaluation (Statics.re:4350-4380, CachedStatics.re:114-121). Elaboration lives inside statics: the separate Elaborator.re was deleted in cc620bbbdc (April 2026). The older Mode and Self modules are also gone (Mode in d22a778d64, Self in ae3f3edde3). Today "mode" is just the ana type, where Unknown(SynSwitch) means "synthesize" (StaticsBase.re:263). "Self" is now elab_syn_ty plus the marks and message that add computes.

Writes to the map are last-write-wins (Map.add_info = Id.Map.add, StaticsBase.re:10-11). A subterm analyzed twice ends up with the second analysis's info. Many cases also run probe analyses whose map they throw away (`let (x, _, _) = go(...)`, e.g. Statics.re:746, 2070, 2091, 2103). Those cost time but leave no trace. The walk also reads its own map back mid-walk: the ModuleExp cls override (2743-2756), the FixF co_ctx patch (2216-2228), reclassify_expanded_module_items, and module_actual_type, which reads the InfoPat of each export. So reading a child's info back out of m, which is what #2651 does, is an existing idiom.

How a let is analyzed on dev (Statics.re:2023-2248):
1. A pattern probe (2052-2053).
2. A probe of the definition in the pattern's context, map discarded (2070). It feeds the structural is_recursive test (2024-2039, 2076).
3. If not recursive: one recorded pass of the definition against p_syn.ty in the outer ctx (2079).
4. If recursive (any let-bound function counts): two more discarded passes and a recorded one in def_ctx, which has the binder in scope (2091, 2103, 2121).
5. The body is analyzed once (2152), then the pattern again with the body's co_ctx, for unused-variable warnings (2154-2155).
6. The let's own elaboration wraps the definition's elaboration: align_exp_if_needed plus add_name (2183-2187). When the definition actually mentions its binder, it gets a FixF fixpoint instead, and the co_ctx at that id is patched (2188-2230).

So on dev any let takes two passes over its definition, and a function let takes four. These multiply when nested. #2603 ("Statics: a let is analyzed once unless it refers to itself", branch dev-statics-perf, commit 4eec302a50) is still OPEN, not merged to dev. It makes non-function definitions take a single pass, and keeps the probe as the final pass for function definitions that neither mention nor shadow their binder.

`module M = def in body` (ModuleExp, Statics.re:2725-2772) is rewritten to a Let. fast_copy re-ids only the new top node, so the Let takes the ModuleExp's id while def and body keep their own ids. That Let goes through the path above: probe plus recorded pass, so two passes over def. Then on dev ModuleExp analyzes def a third time, directly (2757-2762). The only purpose is to get def's elaboration without the Let's align/add_name/FixF wrapping (def_elab_direct). ModuleHelpers.moduleexp_elab then splices that into the Let's elaboration (ModuleHelpers.re:448-456). The third pass also overwrites every info inside def.

#2651 reads def's elab_term back from the InfoExp the Let recorded at Exp.rep_id(def) (29c08fd8fa Statics.re:2775-2789). It falls back to the direct pass in two cases: no info was recorded, or the Let's elaboration is Let(_, FixF, _) (2770-2774). FixF is the only remaining sign that the definition named the module and was analyzed with that name in scope; the co_ctx no longer shows it.

Net passes over a module definition: 3 on dev, 2 with #2651, 1 with #2651 and #2603 together. The ci/statics-passes-dev branch pins that last figure.

One thing for the review: the comment's claim "add records exactly the elab_term it returns" is true of add (Statics.re:268) but not of the whole walk. The singleton-labeled-tuple path (2778-2791 into 310-358) records the unlabeled inner elaboration at the term's ids and returns an unelaborated surface tuple. #2651 reads the recorded one. That is why the new evaluator test gets M.x = 1 where dev gave the unelaborated module. It is a behavior change (an improvement), not a pure refactor.

facts.claim: uexp_to_info_map takes ~ctx, ~ana (default syn), ~is_in_filter, ~ancestors, ~probe_ids, the term and the map, and returns (Info.exp, Exp.t elaboration, Map.t).
`syn` is Unknown(SynSwitch): analyzing against it means synthesize. There is no Mode type on dev; mode is just the ana Typ.t.

Mode.re was deleted in d22a778d64 (2025-04-08, 'delete mode'), Self.re in ae3f3edde3 (2026-04-17), and the separate Elaborator.re in cc620bbbdc (2026-04-17, 'delete elaborator', Matt Keenan). Elaboration now happens inside statics.

add computes the ExpectationMismatch mark from ana vs elab_syn_ty (only when no other marks are present), the inspector message, cls, and ty = fixed_typ(ctx, ana, elab_syn_ty); builds Info.exp; writes it at all ids of user_term; returns (info, elab_term, m).
fixed_typ is the meet of ana and the synthesized type. If the meet fails, it falls back to the synthesized type under synthesis and to ana under analysis.
Map.add_info overwrites (Id.Map.add per id): the last analysis of a subterm determines its recorded info. add_missing_info only fills gaps and is used by Statics.mk for shard ids.
Info.exp fields: user_term, elab_term, ancestors, ctx, ana, elab_syn_ty, marks, co_ctx, probe_targets, cls, message, warnings, ty, label_inference, inferred_label, label_sort, dot_labels.
Info.t variants: InfoDrv, InfoExp, InfoPat, InfoTyp, InfoTPat, InfoMod, InfoSig, InfoMPat, Secondary.
A CoCtx maps each variable name to its uses (use-site id, expected type). CoCtx.mk(ctx_before, ctx_after, co) removes the names a binder added; union concatenates the use lists.
Ctx.t is {use_mode, entries}, where entries holds VarEntry, ConstructorEntry, TVarEntry and LivelitEntry. Extending it conses onto the front, and lookups scan the list.
A Var use records CoCtx.singleton(name, id, ana) and gets Mark.Free(name) when name is not in ctx. That is how an unbound module name becomes an error.
Holes add a '$hole' co_ctx entry, which suppresses unused-variable warnings in enclosing binders.
At the top of every expression's analysis: if ana is a singleton labeled product, the term is first analyzed in synthesis mode (keeping m). If its type does not match, autolabel_singleton_tuple runs.

autolabel_singleton_tuple analyzes a fresh copy against the inner type, then analyzes a surface Tuple([TupLabel(l, copy)]) and discards its elaboration. It records inner_for_source, whose elab_term is the inner elaboration, at the term's own ids, and returns the surface tuple `elaborated_exp`, not an elaboration. Here the recorded elab_term differs from the returned one.
facts.ref: origin/dev src/language/statics/Statics.re:310-358 (discard at 336, record at 357, return at 358)

facts.claim: Fun analyzes its pattern twice: a probe for the body's ctx (map discarded), then again with the body's co_ctx so unused variables can be found. Its co_ctx is CoCtx.mk(ctx, p.ctx, e.co_ctx).
Let on dev: pattern probe; then def_rec_probe, a full analysis of def whose map is discarded; then is_recursive, a structural test (as many pattern vars as functions, and an arrow-like type).
If def is a Tuple and the pattern's type is a Prod, the Let rearranges def's labels before analyzing it. def_rewrap keeps def's ids.

Non-recursive Let: one recorded pass of def in the outer ctx against p_syn.ty. Recursive Let: def_base and def_base2 (both discarded), then a recorded pass in def_ctx with the binder in scope. Counting the probe, that is 2 passes for any let and 4 for a function let.
When def is a Module literal and the pattern binds one name, the Let's body ctx gets a type alias under the module's name for its type exports. Module names therefore live in both namespaces.

The Let's elaboration wraps def's elaboration: Let(p, align_exp_if_needed(...) |> add_name(...), body). Only when requires_fixf (is_rec and the binder appears in def.co_ctx, the body's co_ctx or pat_typ_refs) does it become Let(p, FixF(p, def), body), with the co_ctx at fun_id patched to drop the binder.
A Let's co_ctx is union(def.co_ctx, CoCtx.mk(ctx, p_ana.ctx, body.co_ctx), pat_typ_refs).

#2603 ('Statics: a let is analyzed once unless it refers to itself') is OPEN, not on dev. Its commit 4eec302a50 makes the probe lazy: non-function definitions take a single pass, and a function definition that neither mentions nor shadows its binder keeps the probe as its final analysis.
is_recursive can never be true for a Module literal: get_num_of_functions returns None for Module(_) and ModuleExp(_).
ModuleExp expansion: MPat info first; then pat = mpat_to_pat(mp) (desugars a Sig ascription with Ctx.empty); expanded = fast_copy(rep_id(uexp), Let(pat, def, body)); analyzed with go(~ana).
fast_copy replaces only the top node's ids, so the expanded Let has the ModuleExp's id while def and body keep their own ids. As a result, children of the Let carry ancestors [M_id, M_id, ...].
On dev, ModuleExp then analyzes def a third time, directly, against the Asc type or syn, to get def_elab_direct. This overwrites every info inside def.

moduleexp_elab replaces the Let's (wrapped) def with def_elab_direct and strips the signature Asc from the pattern, so a signature is not enforced at runtime. When expanded_elab is not a Let, it ignores def_elab_direct.
The cls override at the ModuleExp id is redundant: the final add records cls = Exp(Exp.cls_of_term(ModuleExp)) = Exp(ModuleExp) anyway.

def_elab_direct was introduced with the Elaborator deletion. Before that, the old Elaborator elaborated ModuleExp as Let(pat', elaborate(m, def), elaborate(m, body)), reading the statics map rather than re-analyzing.

PR #2651 sets names_itself when the expanded elaboration is Let(_, FixF(_), _). Otherwise it uses the elab_term of the InfoExp at Exp.rep_id(def). It falls back to the old direct analysis when names_itself is set or no InfoExp is found.
Commit e3013b0360 alone lost the error for `module F = fun x -> F(x) in 1`, because the recursive Let analyzed def with F in scope. 29c08fd8fa restores the error and adds a statics test for it.
New evaluator test: `module M : { let x : Int } = { let x = 1; let y = 2 } in M.x` evaluates to 1. Its comment says dev gave the whole unelaborated module.
The incremental evaluator keys reuse on each InfoExp's elab_term and co_ctx. EvalInfo.of_info_map copies them, and reuse_check requires prev_elab to fast_equal info.elab_term.
Statics.mk is memoized on the whole (ana, ctx, term, probe_ids) and returns (map, program elaboration). Subterm re-analyses are not cached.

Module(items) lowers each item to a Let, TyAlias or wildcard Let (wrap_item) around an export tuple, analyzes that in synthesis mode, and builds its type from the exports' InfoPat entries read back from m.

On the CI branch that merges #2603 and #2651, `module M = { let a = 1; let b = a + 1 } in M.b` takes one analysis more than its number of expressions. Each Known case there pins a remaining x3 multiplier: recursive lets, shadowing lets, and label access on an unannotated parameter.

representations.name: Map.t (the info map)
representations.what: Id.Map.t(Info.t): one entry per term id, written last-write-wins.
representations.produced_by: add (Statics.re:268) and the pattern/type/module adds; patched in place by set_marks_exp, patch_elab_syn_ty_exp, the ModuleExp cls override and the FixF co_ctx patch
representations.consumed_by: cursor inspector, error_ids/warning_ids (StaticsBase.re:24-43), completion, EvalInfo.of_info_map for incremental evaluation, and the walk itself reading back (ModuleExp, module_actual_type, and #2651's read-back)

representations.name: Info.exp
representations.what: Per-expression record: user_term, elab_term, ctx, ana, elab_syn_ty, ty, marks, co_ctx, probe_targets, ancestors, message, cls and label fields.
representations.produced_by: add in uexp_to_info_map (Statics.re:249-268); autolabel_singleton_tuple writes inner_for_source (357)
representations.consumed_by: parent cases through the returned info (child.ty, .co_ctx, .elab_syn_ty); the map's consumers above; #2651 reads .elab_term at Exp.rep_id(def)

representations.name: ana (expectation / mode)
representations.what: A Typ.t. Unknown(SynSwitch) means synthesize; anything else means analyze against it. Replaces the deleted Mode module.
representations.produced_by: the parent case, e.g. MatchedTyp.arrow_tolerant for Fun, p_syn.ty for a Let definition, the Asc type for ModuleExp's direct pass
representations.consumed_by: add (mismatch mark, message, fixed_typ); the singleton-labeled-tuple switch (2778); form-specific matching

representations.name: elab_syn_ty / ty
representations.what: elab_syn_ty is the type synthesized for the elaborated term. ty is fixed_typ(ctx, ana, elab_syn_ty), the type after hole fixing. Together with marks and message they replace the deleted Self module.
representations.produced_by: each case passes ~elab_syn_ty to add; add computes ty
representations.consumed_by: parents (e.g. Let uses def.ty as ty_p_ana at 2080, 2092), inspector, module_actual_type

representations.name: marks (Mark.t list)
representations.what: Static errors on a node: Free, ExpectationMismatch, InexhaustiveMatch, BadToken, NoMeet and others. A node with marks is an error (Info.is_error).
representations.produced_by: case-specific marks plus add's expectation_mismatch_mark (StaticsBase.re:335-353)
representations.consumed_by: Map.error_ids, the editor's error display, and tests such as inconsistent_typecheck

representations.name: Ctx.t
representations.what: Typing context: a list of Var, Constructor, TVar and Livelit entries plus use_mode. Extending it conses onto the front.
representations.produced_by: pattern analysis (Var case, Statics.re:3164-3192) and binders such as TyAlias, TypFun and the module export aliases (2124-2151)
representations.consumed_by: Var lookup (691-705), recorded in each Info as ctx, used by completion and get_binding_site

representations.name: CoCtx.t
representations.what: Free-variable uses: name to a list of (use id, expected type). It flows up the tree.
representations.produced_by: Var (singleton), holes ('$hole'), and union/mk at each compound or binder
representations.consumed_by: unused-variable warnings (second pattern pass), the requires_fixf decision (2172-2181), Map.refs_in, the IncrEval reuse map (reuse_map_for_co_ctx)

representations.name: elab_term / returned elaboration
representations.what: The elaborated Exp.t for a node. It is both recorded in the Info and returned up the walk; parents build their own elab_term from the children's returned elabs.
representations.produced_by: each case passes ~elab_term to add, which records and returns the same value. Exception: autolabel_singleton_tuple returns the surface tuple but records the inner elaboration (Statics.re:357-358).
representations.consumed_by: parent elaboration; Statics.mk's program elaboration (evaluator); EvalInfo/IncrEval reuse_check; #2651's def_elab_direct

representations.name: def_elab_direct
representations.what: The ModuleExp definition's elaboration, without the Let's align/add_name/FixF wrapper.
representations.produced_by: dev: a third, direct analysis of def. PR: the recorded InfoExp.elab_term at Exp.rep_id(def), with the direct analysis as fallback.
representations.consumed_by: ModuleHelpers.moduleexp_elab (ModuleHelpers.re:448-456), which builds the ModuleExp's elaboration

representations.name: expanded (ModuleExp to Let)
representations.what: Let(mpat_to_pat(mp), def, body) re-id'd with the ModuleExp's id; def and body keep their own ids.
representations.produced_by: ModuleExp case via fast_copy
representations.consumed_by: the Let case (all type checking of module bindings happens here); expanded_elab feeds names_itself and moduleexp_elab

representations.name: EvalInfo.entry
representations.what: {elab_term, co_ctx, probe_targets} per InfoExp id, the key the incremental evaluator uses for cache reuse.
representations.produced_by: EvalInfo.of_info_map (EvalInfo.re:56-73) from the statics map
representations.consumed_by: IncrEval.reuse_check (IncrEval.re:313-334)

representations.name: lowered (module literal expansion)
representations.what: A Module(items) literal rewritten as nested Let/TyAlias ending in a labeled export tuple, plus its value and type export lists.
representations.produced_by: ModuleHelpers.lower (via wrap_item, 286-317)
representations.consumed_by: the Module case (Statics.re:2701-2723), which analyzes it in synthesis mode and post-processes it with module_elab

Upward arrows from the children labeled '(Info.exp: ty, co_ctx, elab_syn_ty), elab, m'. These feed a box 'add (204-269): mismatch mark, message, ty = fixed_typ'. Dev's direct pass takes the RETURNED arrow -> 'M.x = unelaborated module'. The PR takes the RECORDED arrow -> 'M.x = 1' (test Test_Evaluator_Modules.re:90-96).

review_points: Fix the comment and PR description wording. 'add records exactly the elab_term it returns' (29c08fd8fa Statics.re:2759) is true of add (dev Statics.re:268) but not of uexp_to_info_map. Under a singleton-labeled expectation, autolabel_singleton_tuple records the inner elaboration at the term's ids (357) and returns an unelaborated surface tuple (358). The read-back follows the record, not the return, so the one-member-signature module now evaluates M.x to 1 instead of the raw module. This is a behavior change, an improvement pinned by the new evaluator test. Commit 29c08fd8fa's message says this; the code comment and PR description should too.

Adjacent latent bug, not for this PR: autolabel_singleton_tuple discards the elaboration of its wrapper (Statics.re:336) and returns surface syntax (358). Any term that needs real elaboration (module literals, function-sugar lets, ascription-inserting forms) analyzed against a singleton labeled product that it does not match reaches the evaluator unelaborated. A plain `let` with such an ascription is untouched by #2651 and still hits this. Worth a follow-up issue.

Confirm the editor-visible changes inside a module definition. Infos for def's subterms now come from the Let's pass, not the direct pass. (a) For a function-shaped def (`module F = fun x -> ...`), the Let takes the recursive path, so ctx inside def includes F itself (def_ctx, dev 2102/2121). Completion and hover inside the definition will see F, as they already do for `let f = fun ...`. (b) Ancestors gain a duplicated module id because the expanded Let shares it (fast_copy, 2737-2741). The body already had this on dev. (c) ana is p_syn.ty, the same desugared signature type.

names_itself relies on FixF. FixF appears only when requires_fixf (dev 2172-2181): is_rec, and the binder is in def.co_ctx, the body's co_ctx after removing the binder, or pat_typ_refs. That is conservative: a signature whose types mention the module triggers the fallback too, costing the old extra pass, never a wrong answer. Non-function definitions are never recursive (Exp.re:407-459), so they are analyzed in the outer ctx and the Free mark is already recorded. Please add a test for a module that refers to an earlier module of the same name: `module F = fun x -> x in module F = fun y -> F(y) in F(1)`. It should take the fallback and elaborate non-recursively, as on dev.

The 'no info recorded' fallback looks unreachable on dev. The Let always records def's info in a recording pass (2079 or 2121), and only probes discard their maps. Keeping it as a guard is fine. Reviewers may want a comment or a test-only assertion so a future change that silently falls back (and doubles the cost again) gets noticed.

Interaction with #2603 (open). With #2603, the Let's recorded pass may be the probe (ctx = p_syn.ctx, binder at its synthesized type). An InfoExp at rep_id(def) still exists with the returned elab_term, so the two PRs compose in either merge order. They touch different cases, Let vs ModuleExp, so there should be no textual conflict. ci/statics-passes-dev merges both and pins a module definition at one extra visit in total.

Pass count to state precisely. On dev a module-literal definition is analyzed 3 times: the Let's probe (2070), the Let's pass (2079), and the direct pass (2762). After #2651 alone it is 2, after both PRs 1. The PR description's 'twice' counts only the ModuleExp's own extra pass. Items inside the literal are themselves Lets, so on dev each item's definition gets 3 x 2 = 6 analyses.

A Tuple definition under a signature. The Let rearranges a Tuple def to the pattern's labels before analyzing it (dev 2054-2069); the old direct pass analyzed the original tuple. notes.summary:
On dev, modules are not a separate kind of value. docs/modules.md:5 calls them "a syntactic gloss over labeled tuples". A module body `{ let a = 1; type T = Int; let b = a }` is lowered to an ordinary chain of lets and type aliases ending in a labeled tuple of the exported names: `let a = 1 in type T = Int in let b = a in (a=a, b=b)`. This is done by ModuleHelpers.lower / wrap_item / labeled_tuple_exp, then analyzed by the plain Let and TyAlias code. The module's type is the product of its exported value members (module_actual_type). Member access `M.x` is the ordinary labeled-tuple Dot: in statics it finds the label in the Prod, and at runtime Transition projects the field from the tuple. A signature `{ let x : Int; type T = Int }` is a type that Typ.desugar_sig turns into a labeled product `(x=Int)`; the `type` items in a signature are dropped. A module name enters the context in two ways. As a value, it is a VarEntry made by the let pattern, and its type is the module's product. As a type, it is a TVarEntry alias (Singleton) to the product of the module's type members; this is what makes `M.T` resolve through ProdProjection. A capitalized `M` is parsed as a constructor, and the Constructor case turns it back into Var M when a variable of that name is the newest binding.

`module M = def in body` (ModuleExp) works the same way. Statics builds `let M = def in body` and gives that Let the ModuleExp's own id (fast_copy). The MPat becomes a Pat: Var, or Asc with the signature desugared. Then the Let is analyzed. The Let case analyzes def twice on dev: a recursion probe whose map is discarded (Statics.re:2070), then the real pass that is kept (2079). It then elaborates def as `align_exp_if_needed(ctx, sig, def_elab) |> add_name`, or wraps it in a FixF if def is a function that names its own binder. The ModuleExp case on dev then analyzed def a third time, directly (2757-2762), to get `def_elab_direct`. ModuleHelpers.moduleexp_elab (448-456) builds the runtime term as `Let(pattern with the signature ascription removed, def_elab_direct, body_elab)`. The point of the direct elaboration is to skip what the Let puts around def. The one that matters is the labeled-tuple alignment. A module's elaboration is a let-chain, not a Tuple, so against a one-member signature align_exp wraps the whole module in a one-field tuple, and `M.x` would give back the module instead of 42. The direct elaboration has a history. Matt Keenan's "delete elaborator" commit (cc620bbbdc, April 2026) folded elaboration into statics. The old Elaborator's ModuleExp case elaborated def on its own by reading the info map, and the port turned that into a second full analysis.

PR #2651 ("a module binding analyzes its definition once") drops the third analysis. It reads def's elaboration back from the InfoExp the Let's pass recorded at Exp.rep_id(def). When the Let's elaboration is `Let(_, FixF(_), _)`, meaning the definition names its own module, it still runs the direct analysis, because only that pass reports the name as unbound (the second commit). The read-back relies on "the info at def's id holds the elab the pass returned". That holds for `add` (Statics.re:249-268), but not for autolabel_singleton_tuple (310-359). That path runs when def is checked against a one-label product that its own type does not match, for example a module with more members than its one-member signature. There the info at def's ids is the inner elaboration of the module, while the elab actually returned is a one-field tuple around the *unelaborated* source (`elaborated_exp`). Dev's direct analysis took the returned one, so `M.x` evaluated to the raw Module term, which steps to Indet (Transition.re:1314-1317). The PR reads the info, so `M.x` evaluates to 1. This is the second "corner" in the PR description, and the new evaluator test pins it. In most other cases the read-back gives the same elaboration the direct pass would, because both run in the same ctx with the same expected type. The visible differences are in the infos: for function-valued modules the infos now come from the Let's recursive pass, a tuple def is analyzed in its rearranged form, and the ancestors list differs. After this PR, a module def is still analyzed twice per ModuleExp: by the Let's probe, which the open PR #2603 ("a let is analyzed once unless it refers to itself") removes for non-function defs, and by the Let's real pass. With a one-member signature that matches, the singleton-label pre-pass at Statics.re:2778-2786 doubles each of those passes again.

facts.claim: Expression forms for modules: Module(list(mod_t)) is the `{ ... }` body and ModuleExp(mpat, exp, exp) is `module M = def in body`.

Signatures are a type form Sig(list(sig_t)). Mod items are ModLet/ModType/ModExp/ModuleMod plus hole forms. Sig items are SigLet(pat)/SigType. MPat is Var or Asc(mpat, typ) plus hole forms. Mod, Sig and MPat are sorts of their own in any_t.
The design doc says modules are 'a syntactic gloss over labeled tuples' and that ModuleExp expands to Let during statics.
lower builds the expansion: the items are folded right with wrap_item around a final labeled tuple of the value exports, and type exports are collected separately.

wrap_item turns ModLet into Let, ModType into TyAlias and ModuleMod into Let(mpat_to_pat(mp), def, body), each with the item's own id (fast_copy). A bare expression (ModExp) becomes Let(Wild, e, body) with a fresh id. So a `module` item inside a module body becomes a plain Let and never reaches the ModuleExp case.
Only names that are not shadowed by a later item are exported. The final tuple is (name=name, ...) with fresh ids.

The Module case lowers the items (with ana, so signature member types are put on member patterns), analyzes the expansion in syn mode, reclassifies item infos as Mod, builds the actual Prod type from the export patterns, and records module_elab.
module_elab removes signature ascriptions from let patterns in the expansion and copies the Module's id onto the final tuple. The elaboration's root keeps the first item's id.
Step 1 of the ModuleExp case: record cursor info for the MPat (InfoMPat).

mpat_to_pat gives the resulting Pat the MPat's rep id. Asc desugars the signature with Typ.desugar_sig(Ctx.empty, ...). Anything else becomes Wild. So the Let's pattern info later lands on the MPat's rep id.
Step 2: expanded = fast_copy(rep_id(uexp), Let(pat, def, body)), so the Let has the ModuleExp's id. It is analyzed with the ModuleExp's ana.

Step 3: the cls of the info at the ModuleExp's ids is overridden to ModuleExp. The final add at 2765-2772 writes the same ids again, with cls from Exp.cls_of_term(ModuleExp), so this override is overwritten.

Step 4 on dev: def is analyzed a second time, directly, with ana = the pattern's ascription type or syn. Its returned elab is def_elab_direct, and its infos overwrite those the Let recorded for every node in def.

Step 5: moduleexp_elab takes the Let's elab, keeps its pattern (ascription removed) and body, and swaps in def_elab_direct for the def. If the Let's elab is not a Let, it just removes signature ascriptions and ignores def_elab_direct.

Inside the Let case, def is analyzed once as a recursion probe in p_syn.ctx, and the map from that pass is thrown away. Then it is analyzed again for real (non-recursive path), or three more times (recursive path).

is_recursive needs the number of pattern variables to equal Exp.get_num_of_functions(def). That function returns None for Module and ModuleExp, so a `{...}` module def is never recursive. Only a function-shaped def can be.

What the Let wraps around def: non-recursive gives align_exp_if_needed(ctx, p_syn.ty, def_elab) |> Exp.add_name. Recursive and self-referring gives FixF(p, def) under the function's id, and the info at that id has the bound names removed from its co_ctx.

align_exp wraps any non-Tuple expression in a one-field tuple when the expected type has a single labeled field. A module elaboration's root is a Let, so against a one-member signature it becomes (x = <whole module>). This wrapping is what def_elab_direct avoids.
dev already has an evaluator test showing the direct elaboration matters: `module M : { let x : Int } = { let x = 42 } in M.x` evaluates to 42.
add records an Info.exp whose elab_term is the same elab_term it returns.

Exception to that: when ana is a one-label product that the term's own type does not match, autolabel_singleton_tuple runs. It analyzes a fresh copy against the inner type, records inner_for_source (the inner elab) at the term's ids, and returns `elaborated_exp`, a one-field tuple around the unelaborated term.

In the singleton-label wrapper, the syn pre-pass's map is rebound, but default_case closes over the original m. When the label matches, the pre-pass's work is thrown away, so every term checked against a one-label product is analyzed twice.
An unelaborated Module or ModuleExp that reaches dynamics steps to Indet.

PR: names_itself is true when the expanded Let's elab is Let(_, FixF(_), _). Unless names_itself, def_elab_direct is read from the InfoExp at Exp.rep_id(def). The direct analysis runs only as the fallback.
PR tests: `module F = fun x -> F(x) in 1` must be a static error, and `module M : { let x : Int } = { let x = 1; let y = 2 } in M.x` must evaluate to 1.
Module name as a value: the pattern Var case adds VarEntry{name, id = pattern rep id (= MPat id), typ}.

Module name as a type: when def is Module(items) with type members, the body ctx gets Ctx.extend_alias(name, Prod of type exports). When def is a variable or capitalized name that already has such an alias, the alias is copied (module aliasing).
Ctx has VarEntry, ConstructorEntry, TVarEntry (kind Singleton or Abstract) and LivelitEntry. There is no entry kind for modules.
A capitalized `M` is parsed as Constructor. If the newest binding of the name is a variable (newest_var_or_ctr), or no constructor exists, it elaborates to Var(M) and gets the variable's type.
Value member access: Dot analyzes the left side, normalizes its type to a Prod, finds the label (LabelNotFound otherwise), and elaborates to Dot(e1_elab, label).
Type member access: M.T is ProdProjection(Var M, Label T). weak_head_normalize resolves Var M through lookup_alias and projects the field.
Signature to type: desugar_sig keeps only SigLet items as labeled fields and drops SigType. The pattern Asc case uses it for the expected type and elaborates to Asc(p, normalize(ann)).
At runtime, Dot projects the labeled field out of a tuple value.

The elab the evaluator runs is the root elab that statics returns (Statics.mk), not one read from the map. InfoExp.elab_term is still consumed by EvalInfo and by the incremental evaluator's reuse check.

History: def_elab_direct and the second go() came in with 'delete elaborator' (Matt Keenan, cc620bbbdc). The old Elaborator elaborated ModuleExp as Let(pat', elaborate(m, def), elaborate(m, body)), reading the info map.
docs/modules.md still describes an Elaborator.re that does 'permanent expansion for evaluation'. That file was deleted in cc620bbbdc.

The elaboration test for a one-member signature on a plain let compares against `let m : (x=Int) = (let x = 1 in (x=x)) in m`. Both sides go through the same Let alignment, so it cannot detect wrapping.
PR #2603 ('a let is analyzed once unless it refers to itself') is still OPEN.

review_points: The read-back depends on one invariant: 'the InfoExp at rep_id(def) holds the elab the Let used for def'. The code comment states it as 'add records exactly the elab_term it returns' (29c08fd8fa Statics.re:2759). That is true of add (Statics.re:249-268) but not of autolabel_singleton_tuple (310-359), where the info is the inner elab and the returned elab is an unelaborated one-field wrapper. That gap causes corner 2, and the new evaluator test (Test_Evaluator_Modules.re:86-96 @29c08fd8fa) now pins it. Decide whether to keep a test whose result depends on this gap, or fix autolabel to return an elaborated wrapper separately. Either way, the comment should name the exception.

The fallback 'when no info was recorded' is effectively unreachable. Every uexp_to_info_map ends in add at the term's ids, so the fallback really only serves names_itself. The comment and PR text could say that, so nobody relies on it as a safety net.

names_itself detects self-reference from the shape of the Let's elab (Let(_, FixF, _)). That matches requires_fixf (Statics.re:2172-2181, 2229) only while the expanded Let is not autolabeled. When it is autolabeled, moduleexp_elab ignores def_elab_direct anyway (ModuleHelpers.re:454), so it is safe, but it is coupled to the Let's elaboration shape. A sturdier signal would be for the Let to report is_rec/requires_fixf some other way. Worth a question to Alexander about which he would prefer to maintain.

Function-valued modules that do not name themselves (`module F = fun x -> ? in ...`) take the Let's recursive path (one variable, one function), so def is analyzed in def_ctx with F bound. Dev's direct pass overwrote those infos using the outer ctx. With the PR they stay, so the cursor inspector and completions inside the function now list F as in scope, and using F then turns names_itself on and becomes an error. This is a small editor-facing change. If #2603 merges, its probe in p_syn.ctx has the same effect. There is also no test that pins the read-back on this path; something like `module F = fun x -> x + 1 in F(2)` evaluating to 3 would.

Smaller info differences to sanity-check, all present on dev for body infos already. (1) def's infos now carry the ModuleExp id twice in ancestors, because the expanded Let reuses that id (Statics.re:270, 2737-2742). (2) A Tuple def with a labeled-product signature is analyzed in its rearranged form (Statics.re:2054-2069), so its label-inference message can change.

Architecture question for Modules II: def_elab_direct exists only to keep a module's let-chain elaboration out of align_exp's one-field wrapping (LabeledTupleHelpers.re:49-75). The plain-let form `let m : { let x : Int } = { let x = 1 } in m.x`, and a `module N : {one member} = {...}` item inside a module body (lowered to a plain Let by wrap_item, ModuleHelpers.re:300-304), go through the Let's alignment with no such guard. By reading the code they likely evaluate to a wrapped module rather than the member. This is unverified; a one-line CLI probe at dev would settle it. Test_Elaboration.re:799-809 cannot catch it. If align_exp could see through a Let/TyAlias chain to its final tuple, as restore_module_body_id already does (ModuleHelpers.re:375-386), then the ModuleExp could use the Let's elaboration as is, and both def_elab_direct and this PR's read-back would go away.

Repeat analysis this PR leaves in place for module defs: the Let's recursion probe at Statics.re:2070 (removed for non-function defs by the open #2603), and the singleton-label pre-pass at 2778-2790, whose map is discarded because default_case closes over the original m. A module under a matching one-member signature is still analyzed twice per pass. Both are the same 'statics re-analyzes whole subterms' finding as #2609 item 7 ('Performance Challenges (Fall 2026)'), and each extra pass multiplies with nesting.

Pre-existing and not caused by the PR: the cls override at Statics.re:2743-2756 is overwritten by the final add at 2765-2772, which writes the same ids with cls ModuleExp. docs/modules.md:261-264 and :300 still describe the deleted Elaborator.re. The double analysis came from cc620bbbdc (the 'delete elaborator' commit) porting the old Elaborator's 'elaborate def directly from the map'. The PR's read-back returns to that original design, and a sentence in the PR or the docs saying so would help reviewers.

Sound as long as the PR keeps both: the final ModuleExp info still takes co_ctx, probe_targets and elab_syn_ty from the expanded Let, as on dev (dev discarded the direct pass's co_ctx too), so the co_ctx used for reuse is the same. In the non-self-referring case, def_elab_direct is now physically the same term as the InfoExp elab_term at def's id, which the incremental evaluator's reuse check reads (IncrEval.re:328-334).

notes.summary:
What the evaluator gets. On dev, the statics pass (Statics.mk → uexp_to_info_map) produces two things. The first is the elaborated program: a single Exp.t. DHExp is just `include Exp`, so there is no separate runtime term type. The second is the info_map, where every expression id has an InfoExp holding its own elab_term, co_ctx (free variables) and probe_targets. The editor keeps both in CachedStatics. EvalResult.calculate sends a new evaluation only when the root elaboration changes under fast_equal_with_lexemes (ids are ignored), or when settings or probe targets change. It also cuts the info_map down to EvalInfo.t, which holds per id {elab_term, co_ctx, probe_targets} plus the probe targets. The full info_map cannot cross postMessage because LivelitCtx entries contain closures. A worker request is a batch of (key, {expr = root elaboration, eval_info_map, prev = last run's incremental cache}), Marshal-encoded. The worker replies in four steps: an instant Ack; a ReusePlan (the reuse pre-pass, run only when EvalInfo has at least 2500 entries); Stream updates after each 5000-step slice; and finally a Result holding (key, Ok((value Exp.t, EvaluatorState.t)) | Error) plus eval_time. EvaluatorState carries probes, tests, theorems and incr_eval. The client turns it into Dynamics.t {probe_map, test_results, theorems} and keeps incr_eval as `prev` for the next request.

How modules run. There is no module value type such as ModVal. A module is lowered in statics into a chain of lets that ends in a labeled tuple (x = x, y = y). `module M = def in body` becomes `let M = def in body`. At runtime M is bound in the environment like any other let, and `M.x` is the Dot transition doing labeled-tuple projection. Signatures are removed before runtime: ascriptions on member patterns and on the module pattern are stripped, so nothing is sealed when the program runs. If a raw Module or ModuleExp ever reaches the evaluator, it is Indet (stuck). Ids decide what the evaluator records and reuses. Ids on surface nodes are deterministic: each member's let takes the item's id, and the export tuple takes the def's id. But every lowering mints fresh ids for the export-tuple field nodes.

What evaluation depends on from statics: (1) the root elaboration, which is the program actually run; (2) EvalInfo per id: elab_term + co_ctx + probe_targets are the keys of incremental reuse (IncrEval.reuse_check). Reuse compares this run's recorded elab_term at an id with last run's; it does not compare against the subtree the evaluator meets at that id. is_program_node also uses EvalInfo to decide what gets streamed; (3) probe targets, built from info_map co_ctx/ctx through refs_in, which decide where samples are recorded; (4) the count of EvalInfo entries, which decides incremental vs from-scratch. So a change in elaboration matters downstream in two ways: if the root elaboration changes, the program's behaviour changes; if the recorded elab_term or co_ctx at an id stops describing what runs at that id, reuse can be stale or never hit.

What #2651 changes downstream. For ordinary module bindings the root elaboration should be structurally the same as on dev. In the usual cases the Let analyzes the def with the same context and expected type as the old second analysis did. What changes is that the info at def.id and the def slot in the ModuleExp elaboration are now one value by construction. Also, the leftover InfoExp entries from the first lowering go away: on dev that lowering's elaboration was thrown out, but its fresh-id entries stayed in info_map. This makes EvalInfo and the worker payload smaller, and it can move a program across the 2500-entry incremental threshold. One case does change at runtime: a module under a one-member signature whose def synthesizes a different product. The Let's analysis records, at def.id, an inner elaboration (from autolabel_singleton_tuple) that is different from the elaboration it returns. On dev, M was bound to a tuple wrapping the raw, unelaborated Module, so M.x was Indet. Now M is the full module tuple, unsealed, and M.x is 1. The second commit (the names_itself check for FixF) matters for dynamics as well as for the error mark. In the FixF branch, the Let's recorded info at def.id is a plain Fun whose co_ctx has had the module name removed. Reading that back would put a non-recursive Fun in the slot without the name in its co_ctx, so reuse could ignore changes to an outer binding of that name. The fallback re-analysis overwrites that info.

facts.claim: DHExp is not a separate type: DHExp.re includes Exp, so the evaluator consumes the same Exp.t data structure that statics elaborates into.
Statics.mk returns (info_map, root elaboration), memoized on (ana, ctx, term, probe_ids), with a post-pass copying info to sibling shard ids.
CachedStatics stores term, elaborated, info_map, error/warning ids and probe targets; elaborated is replaced by a dummy Var when statics or dynamics+elaboration are off.

Probe targets are computed from info_map: each probed expression id captures Statics.Map.refs_in, which maps the info's co_ctx through its ctx to binding ids; with probe_all every InfoExp/InfoPat id is a target.
Statics `add` records an InfoExp whose elab_term is exactly the elab it returns; every node's info carries cls, ana, ty, ctx, co_ctx, probe_targets, ancestors, user_term, elab_term.

Exception to 'add records what it returns': autolabel_singleton_tuple returns elaborated_exp = Tuple([TupLabel(l, original_expression)]) where original_expression is the RAW user term with a fresh root id, but records inner_for_source (the inner analysis against the field type) at the source term's ids.
The singleton-label lift wraps EVERY expression node: if ana normalizes to a one-field labeled Prod and the synthesized type is not that label, autolabel_singleton_tuple is used.

On dev the ModuleExp case expands to Let(mpat_to_pat(mp), def, body) with the ModuleExp's id, analyzes it, then analyzes def a second time directly (def_ana = ascribed type or syn) and splices that elaboration into the Let's def slot via moduleexp_elab.

The PR replaces the direct analysis with a read-back of InfoExp.elab_term at Exp.rep_id(def), unless the expanded elaboration is Let(_, FixF(_), _) (names_itself) or no InfoExp exists; then it falls back to the old direct analysis.
moduleexp_elab rebuilds Let(strip_module_sig_pats_in_pat(p), def_elab_direct, body_elab); if the expanded elaboration is not a Let it ignores def_elab_direct and just strips signature patterns.
The Let case on dev analyzes def once as a throwaway (def_rec_probe, map discarded) and once for real; so a module def was analyzed three times on dev, and after #2651 twice (#2603 is not on dev).

The Let elaboration wraps def: align_exp_if_needed + Exp.add_name in the non-recursive path; in the recursive-and-self-referencing path a FixF placed at fun_id = rep_id(def_elab), with the inner Fun given a derived id.

In the FixF branch the InfoExp at fun_id is rewritten with co_ctx = CoCtx.mk(ctx, p_ana.ctx, info.co_ctx), i.e. the recursive name removed, because the FixF binds it; its elab_term stays the plain Fun.
Module lowering: each item becomes a Let/TyAlias carrying the item's Mod id; the final export is a labeled tuple whose Tuple, TupLabel, Label and Var nodes are all Exp.fresh (new ids every lowering).
Exp.fresh mints a new unique id from a monotonic counter plus session-random bits; ids are not derived from the source term.
module_elab strips signature ascriptions from member let patterns and copies the Module expression's id onto the export Tuple; the Module's info records that as elab_term.
Module access M.x elaborates to Dot(e1_elab, label) and runs as labeled-tuple projection: req_final both sides, unbox LabeledTupleProjection, pick the matching TupLabel field.
There is no module value form at runtime: if a raw Module or ModuleExp reaches the evaluator it is Indet ('should be expanded before reaching dynamics').
Let evaluation: requires def final, pattern-matches, extends the environment, steps to Closure(env', body); it emits RecordPatMatch{pat, rhs: d1 (the unevaluated def), samples}.
Var lookup copies the environment entry with a fresh id; FixF and Let entries are not treated as final values.
FixF in environment mode first captures its env, then unwraps by binding the name(s) to the fixpoint and stepping into the body.
EvalInfo is the serializable slice of statics the evaluator uses: statics: Id.Map(entry{elab_term, co_ctx, probe_targets}) plus targets; of_info_map keeps only InfoExp entries.
is_program_node(id) = id has an EvalInfo entry; the evaluator uses it to decide which top-level ids may publish to the streaming outbox.

Evaluator pipeline per node: eval_5 (separate state per top-level expr) -> eval_4 (reuse check / record incr entry) -> eval_3 (probe span open/close if id in targets) -> eval_2 (until final) -> eval_1 (EvaluatorState.update with side effects) -> eval_0 (Transition).

reuse_check hits only at top level (empty call stack) when: a prev entry exists at the id, EvalInfo's elab_term at that id is fast_equal (ids ignored) with lexemes equal to the prev entry's prev_elab, the reuse_map restricted to the info's co_ctx matches, and probe targets match.

On a cache miss at top level the evaluator records an incr entry keyed by the id, snapshotting EvalInfo's elab_term, co_ctx-restricted reuse_map and probe_targets with the computed value and replay state.
Reuse provenance for a let-bound name comes from RecordPatMatch: source = rep_id of the rhs expression, flag Clean iff that id was reused.
Reuse tracking and the reuse pre-pass run only if prev is non-empty or EvalInfo has statics; results are finished by substituting the env and replacing all ids.

EvalResult re-requests evaluation only when the root elaboration changes under fast_equal_with_lexemes, or settings/targets change; EvalInfo is rebuilt on the main thread because LivelitCtx closures cannot cross postMessage.

Worker request value = {expr: Exp.t, eval_info_map: EvalInfo.t, prev: incr_eval}; a request is {request_id, batch: list((key, value))}; response per key is Result((Exp.t, EvaluatorState.t), ProgramResult.error).
Server messages: Ack{request_id} (liveness), ReusePlan{request_id, initial: (key, IncrEval.t) list}, Stream{request_id, key, update: IncrEval.outbox}, Result{request_id, response, eval_time}.
Both directions are Marshal-encoded strings (the #2368 fix for structured-clone overflow on deep payloads).

Worker phases: on_request posts Ack immediately and enters Planning; the next slice posts ReusePlan; then items run as yielding evaluations in 5000-trampoline-step slices scheduled by setTimeout(0), flushing Stream updates, then Result; a newer request abandons stale slices.
Incremental mode only applies to items whose EvalInfo has >= 2500 entries; below that the worker passes an empty prev and skips the reuse pre-pass.
Client: ack timeout 5 s (15 s cold start), up to 3 retries with worker restart; whole-request timeout 20 s restarts the worker and reports Timeout; messages for superseded request ids are dropped.
EvalRequest maps worker callbacks to EvalResult actions: Result -> UpdateResult, ReusePlan -> UpdateStreamingEval, Stream -> MergeStreamingEval.
Without a worker the same evaluation runs synchronously on the main thread via WorkerServer.evaluate_sync, which clears transient state before returning.
EvaluatorState is a write-only log: theorems, tests, probes (Sample.Map), obs_opens/obs_trace (observation spans), step_count, incr_eval.
The UI turns EvaluatorState into Dynamics.t {probe_map, test_results, theorems} and saves state.incr_eval as next request's prev.
Pending-eval UI ids are computed from info_map (top-level leaves by parent user_term and ancestors), not from the elaboration.
The PR's new evaluator test asserts that `module M : { let x : Int } = { let x = 1; let y = 2 } in M.x` runs to 1 (comment: before #2651 M.x was the whole unelaborated module).
Evaluator tests elaborate via Statics.mk and run Evaluator.evaluate with no eval_info and no prev, so incremental reuse and probe recording are not exercised.

Statics.mk forks into [root elaboration Exp.t] and [info_map: id -> InfoExp{elab_term, co_ctx, probe_targets, ctx}]. Both go into [CachedStatics {elaborated, info_map, targets}] -> [EvalResult.calculate]. A diamond gate inside it is labeled 'elab changed? (fast_equal_with_lexemes, ids ignored) or settings/targets changed'. Two side arrows: info_map -> [EvalInfo.of_info_map] -> 'eval_info_map', and info_map -> [compute_targets] -> 'targets'. Then [Request {expr, eval_info_map, prev}] -> 'Marshal + postMessage' crossing into the worker lane -> [Evaluator] -> [Result (value, EvaluatorState)] -> back across -> [Dynamics.t {probe_map, tests, theorems}]. A dashed arrow 'state.incr_eval saved as prev' loops back into the next Request. Color the two arrows that #2651 touches: 'def slot of ModuleExp elab' inside the root elaboration, and 'InfoExp at def.id' inside info_map.

ModuleExp elaboration on dev vs #2651, two columns. Shared top: [module M = def in body] -> 'expand' -> [Let(M, def, body) with ModuleExp id] -> 'go (Let analysis)' -> [records InfoExp at def.id: elab_term E1] and [expanded_elab = Let(p, wrap(E1), body_elab), where wrap = align + add_name, or FixF]. A diamond before it, 'expanded_elab is Let(_, FixF, _) or no InfoExp?', has a 'yes' arrow back to the dev-style box. Bottom label: 'root elab -> evaluator; info map -> EvalInfo'.
