review_points: For an ordinary module binding, check that the root elaboration really does not change. The old second analysis used ana = def_ana (the ascribed type or syn) in the outer ctx. The Let's analysis uses ana = p_syn.ty and, for non-recursive lets, the same outer ctx. Compare Statics.re:2050-2051, 2079 (dev) with PR Statics.re:2782-2786. For Var patterns both are Unknown(SynSwitch). For an Asc pattern, p_syn.ty should be the ascribed signature type, but this is worth confirming. Cheap check: elaborate a few module programs on both commits and compare them with Exp.fast_equal_with_lexemes. This is also the exact gate that decides whether EvalResult re-requests evaluation (EvalResult.re:255).

The one runtime change, the one-member signature case, comes from autolabel_singleton_tuple (Statics.re:310-358). It records inner_for_source at the def's ids, but returns a tuple that wraps the raw user term. So the PR comment's 'add records exactly the elab_term it returns' does not always hold, and this exception is the one that turns M.x from Indet into 1. Decide whether this is the intended semantics. M is now the full, unsealed 2-member tuple, because signatures are stripped before runtime (ModuleHelpers.re:341-371, 452). So M.y would presumably also run. One test pinning this down would document it.

A related bug is on dev and outside this PR. autolabel_singleton_tuple returns an elaboration that contains the raw, unelaborated term (Statics.re:329-334, 357). Any Module or ModuleExp that ends up inside that elaboration evaluates to Indet (Transition.re:1314-1321). For example, a `module ... in ...` expression analyzed against a one-label tuple type with a different label. #2651 fixes only the def-slot instance. Worth an issue.

The second commit matters for incremental reuse as well as for the error mark. In the FixF branch the Let rewrites the InfoExp at fun_id: co_ctx drops the module name and elab_term is a plain Fun (Statics.re:2208-2229). Read back without the FixF guard, this would put a non-recursive Fun in the slot whose co_ctx is missing a name it actually uses. reuse_check (IncrEval.re:336-341) would then ignore changes to an outer binding of that name, so a cached closure could be reused stale. The fallback re-analysis overwrites that info. Check that the guard catches every way FixF can be placed: Var or Asc patterns, tuple patterns of functions, defs wrapped in parens.

names_itself looks only at the top shape of expanded_elab (PR Statics.re:2770-2774). If the ModuleExp itself is analyzed against a one-label product with a different label, the Let is wrapped by the singleton lift (Statics.re:2775-2791). names_itself is then false and the read-back happens. moduleexp_elab ignores def_elab_direct in that case (ModuleHelpers.re:454), so the root elaboration is unaffected. But the info at def.id keeps the Let's recursive analysis, including the patched co_ctx and no unbound-name error. Very rare; worth a sentence in the PR or a TODO.

EvalInfo shrinks. On dev the Let's lowering of the def was thrown out, but its fresh-id InfoExp entries stayed in info_map: export Tuple/TupLabel/Label/Var nodes (ModuleHelpers.re:162-171) and Let(Wild) wrappers (299-316). They then went into EvalInfo and the Marshal'd worker request. Every subtree of the Let's analysis was also redone. Downstream effects: a smaller postMessage payload. A program near incremental_min_statics = 2500 (WorkerServer.re:300-304) can switch between incremental and from-scratch evaluation. And with probe_all, fewer orphan targets (CachedStatics.re:43-48). None of this should change results.

Incremental reuse is keyed on what the info_map recorded at an id, not on the subtree the evaluator actually meets there (IncrEval.re:326-334). The PR makes info[def.id].elab_term and the ModuleExp's def slot the same value by construction, which is a good invariant to state in the PR. Note that for a non-empty Module def, the slot's root node has the first item's id (wrap_item, ModuleHelpers.re:290-292), and def.id sits on the export Tuple (restore_module_body_id, 375-386). This is unchanged by the PR, but it is how a reviewer should read reuse and provenance for M (RecordPatMatch rhs id, Transition.re:549-556; ReusePass.re:38-45).

Test coverage: the new evaluator test runs Evaluator.evaluate with no eval_info and no prev (Test_Evaluator_Prelude.re:25-28, 126-142). It does not exercise reuse, probes or the worker path. A probe inside a module def would check that samples still land on surface ids. A two-run incremental test would cover the read-back: edit the body, check that the module binding is reused (entry at the first item's id / def.id) and that an edit inside the def invalidates it.

Performance claim on dev: a module def was analyzed three times: the throwaway def_rec_probe at Statics.re:2070, the main Let analysis at 2079, and the direct analysis at 2762. #2651 removes the third, and #2603 (not on dev) targets the first kind. Because nested module defs repeat the work, the saving compounds with depth. Evaluation step counts should be unchanged; a step-count or probe step-range diff on a module-heavy example would confirm the evaluator sees an identical program.

notes.summary:
What this code is. Hazel's statics (uexp_to_info_map in src/language/statics/Statics.re) walks an expression and returns three things: an info record for the root, the root's elaborated term, and an updated info map. The info map is a persistent Id.Map that holds an Info record for every node. The cursor inspector, probes and the evaluator all read it. `module M = def in body` (a ModuleExp) has no typing rule of its own. The ModuleExp case turns it into `let M = def in body`: the pattern comes from ModuleHelpers.mpat_to_pat, and the new Let is given the module's own id. The ordinary Let case then type-checks it. The module's elaboration is not the Let's, though. ModuleHelpers.moduleexp_elab rebuilds `Let(pattern without its signature, def_elab_direct, body_elab)`, which throws away everything the Let wrapped around def: label alignment, a function name and, for a function that calls itself, a FixF fixpoint. A module is not meant to be recursive. So dev got def_elab_direct by analyzing def one more time, directly, in the outer context (Statics.re:2757-2762). That pass also overwrote the Let's info for every node inside def.

What the PR changes. Commit e3013b0360 drops that extra pass and looks the result up instead. When the Let analyzed def, def's own `add` wrote an InfoExp at def's ids. Its elab_term is the same value `add` returned to the Let, taken before the Let applied align_exp_if_needed, add_name or FixF. So right after `go(~ana, expanded, m)` returns, the ModuleExp case reads `Id.Map.find_opt(Exp.rep_id(def), m)` and uses that elab_term. The map is persistent and passed along explicitly, and passes whose maps are thrown away (the Let's recursion probe) never reach it. So the entry found is the one this same invocation's Let wrote. The direct pass stays as the fallback branch. Commit 29c08fd8fa adds one guard. If the Let's elaboration has the shape `Let(_, FixF(...), _)`, the Let analyzed def with the module's own name in scope, so a self-reference produced no error. In that case the old direct pass runs again and reports the name as unbound, as dev does. The Let also strips the name from the co_ctx of def's info (Statics.re:2216-2228), so that co_ctx can't be used as the signal; the FixF is. The commit adds two tests: one for a definition that names its own module, one for a module under a one-member signature.

Why it is equivalent, and where it is not. In the Let's non-recursive branch (Statics.re:2079), the Let's pass and dev's direct pass call the same function. The ctx is the same (the ModuleExp's). The expected type is the same: p_syn.ty is the meet of `syn` with the Asc type (or with an unknown), and since desugar_sig ignores ctx and is idempotent, that equals the direct pass's def_ana. The term is the same, unless the Let's tuple rearrangement rewrote a tuple-literal def. is_in_filter and probe_ids are the same. Only the ancestors list differs: the module's id appears twice, as it already does for the body. So the elaborations match whenever the info def records equals the elab it returns. Every path that ends in `add` does that (Statics.re:249-268). The one exception is the singleton-label lift (autolabel_singleton_tuple, Statics.re:310-358). It records the inner elaboration at def's ids but returns raw relabeled syntax, and that is exactly the one-member-signature corner. On dev, `module M : { let x : Int } = { let x = 1; let y = 2 } in M.x` evaluated to unelaborated module source; with the PR it evaluates to 1. The PR keeps this change and pins it with a test. In the recursive branch without FixF (a function-valued module that does not name itself), the elaboration is the same, but the info for nodes inside def now has a ctx that includes the module's own name. The editor can show that; the elaboration does not depend on it.

Cost and status. On today's dev, a plain module definition is analyzed three times per module binding: the Let's recursion probe (2070, always run), the Let's real pass (2079), and the ModuleExp's direct pass (2762). The PR makes it two. It reaches one only together with #2603 ("a let is analyzed once unless it refers to itself"), which is still open. Function-valued modules go from 5 passes to 4, and a module that names itself stays at 5. Before (dev): the ModuleExp case writes MPat info, builds `Let(pat, def, body)` carrying the module's own id via IdTagged.fast_copy, and type-checks it with the ordinary Let case.

Before (dev): the case then analyzes def a second time, directly, in the ModuleExp's ctx, with def_ana = the signature type if the pattern is Asc, else syn. That pass also overwrites the Let's info for every node inside def.

moduleexp_elab rebuilds the Let's elaboration with def_elab_direct in place of the Let's def, which may be aligned, named or FixF-wrapped, and strips the signature from the pattern. If the expanded elab is not a Let, it ignores def_elab_direct entirely.
After (PR): names_itself is true exactly when expanded_elab.term matches `Let(_, {term: FixF(_), _}, _)`.

After (PR): def_elab_direct is the elab_term of the InfoExp found at Exp.rep_id(def) in the map returned by the Let, unless names_itself holds. If it holds, or no InfoExp is found, the old direct pass runs unchanged, with def_ana = Asc type or syn.

`add` builds the Info.exp with elab_term set to the elab_term it was given, writes it at all of the user_term's ids, and returns that same elab_term. This is the 'add records exactly what it returns' property the PR relies on.

Exception to that property: autolabel_singleton_tuple returns the raw syntax `rewrap(Tuple([TupLabel(Label l, original_expression)]))`, not an elaboration. Its last write at the expression's ids is inner_for_source, whose elab_term is the inner elaboration of a fresh copy analyzed against the label's type. So for this path, recorded elab != returned elab.

The singleton lift fires whenever the expected type is a one-field labeled product and the expression's synthesized type is neither that one-field product nor unknown. A one-member signature `{ let x : Int }` desugars to exactly such a product.

The Let case analyzes def several times. A recursion probe in p_syn.ctx always runs and its map is discarded. Then either one real pass in the outer ctx (non-recursive), or def_base and def_base2 (maps discarded) followed by a real pass in def_ctx with the bound name in scope (recursive). Only the real pass's writes stay in m.

is_recursive needs the pattern's variable count to equal the number of functions in def and an arrow-like type. A Module(items) literal is never 'recursive'. Only a function-valued (or one-function-tuple) module definition takes the recursive branch.

FixF is used only when is_rec and the bound name appears in def's co_ctx (or in pattern type refs). CoCtx.mk filters the pattern's own bindings out of the body's co_ctx, so a use in the body alone does not trigger it.

The Let applies align_exp_if_needed and Exp.add_name to def's elab (and FixF in the recursive case) only after def's info was recorded. So the recorded elab_term is the unwrapped elaboration, the same thing the direct pass returns.
In the FixF case the Let rewrites the info at fun_id (= def's rep id) to drop the bound name from its co_ctx, leaving elab_term unchanged. This is why the info's co_ctx cannot reveal self-reference.

The Let's own co_ctx is union(def.co_ctx, ...), where def is the unpatched info returned by the real pass. So expanded_info.co_ctx still contains the bound name when def mentions it: a second, unused signal.

The expected type matches. mpat_to_pat already applies Typ.desugar_sig(Ctx.empty, typ). The pattern's Asc case uses desugar_sig(ctx, ann.user_term), which ignores ctx and is idempotent. p_syn.ty = fixed_typ(ctx, syn, ann_ty) = meet(Unknown SynSwitch, ann_ty) = ann_ty. For a bare Var pattern, meet(SynSwitch, SynSwitch) = SynSwitch = syn.

The Let rewrites def before analyzing it only when def is a tuple literal and the pattern's type is a product (label rearrangement with fresh TupLabel nodes, ids kept via def_rewrap). The Tuple case rearranges its elaboration against a product the same way, so this can differ from the direct pass only in fresh ids and label-inference info.
Statics.mk starts every run from Id.Map.empty, and passes inside one run thread a persistent map. So no stale info from an earlier run or a discarded pass can be what the read-back finds.

Module items of the form `module N = def` inside `{ ... }` are lowered to a plain Let, not a ModuleExp. So the read-back and the self-naming guard apply only to expression-level `module M = def in body`, and by reading, a self-naming module item is analyzed (and elaborated) recursively with FixF.
The 'Override cls to show Module binding' block is redundant. The ModuleExp's final `add` recomputes cls from uexp.term, which is already Exp(ModuleExp). This is pre-existing and untouched by the PR.
Duplicate adjacent ancestor ids already occur, and at least one consumer works around them. The PR gives def's nodes ancestors [module id, module id, ...], the same shape the body already has.
The self-naming test uses inconsistent_typecheck, which only asserts that the list of static errors is non-empty anywhere in the program. It does not pin the error's place or kind.
The new evaluator test checks that `module M : { let x : Int } = { let x = 1; let y = 2 } in M.x` evaluates to 1. The existing exact-signature case (`= { let x = 42 }`, giving 42) sits next to it.
No test reaches the fallback with a signature-ascribed pattern (no `module F : ... = fun ...` anywhere in test/). That arm is the likeliest owner of the one patch line codecov reports uncovered.

review_points: The equivalence rests on two facts: same inputs, and the info a node records equals the elab it returns. Check both in the Let's non-recursive branch (Statics.re:2079 vs dev 2762): same ctx, same expected type (p_syn.ty vs def_ana, by desugar_sig idempotence and meet(SynSwitch, T) = T), same term, same is_in_filter and probe_ids, different ancestors only. The second fact holds for paths ending in `add` (249-268). It does NOT hold for autolabel_singleton_tuple (310-358), so the PR description's 'add records exactly the elab_term it returns' should say 'every path that ends in add'. The singleton-label lift is the one known exception.

One-member-signature corner (a behavior change, kept): `module M : { let x : Int } = { let x = 1; let y = 2 } in M.x` now evaluates to 1 instead of raw module source. Alexander should confirm this is the intended runtime meaning of a too-wide module under a signature, given test_limitation_extra_member_multi (Test_Statics_Modules.re:382-387) treats it as a static error.

names_itself checks the shape of the Let's elaboration (Let(_, FixF, _)). That ties the ModuleExp case to where the Let case puts the FixF (Statics.re:2188-2230). If the Let later wraps the FixF in something else, the check silently turns false and self-naming errors disappear again; test_module_names_itself is the only guard. Consider an explicit signal instead. One exists: expanded_info.co_ctx contains the bound name when def mentions it (Statics.re:2235-2240), which is conservative and also fires for non-recursive self-reference.

The 'no info recorded' arm of the fallback is effectively unreachable. Every uexp_to_info_map call writes an InfoExp at its root's ids, and maps are rebuilt from empty each run (Statics.re:4350-4362). It is defensive, not a real path; the comment at 29c08fd8fa 2757-2763 suggests otherwise.

Semantics question for Alexander (Modules II): an expression-level `module F = fun x -> F(x) in 1` is an error (F unbound), but the same item inside a module, `{ module F = fun x -> F(x) }`, is lowered to a plain Let (ModuleHelpers.re:300-304). By reading, that one is analyzed and elaborated recursively with FixF and no error. The new test's comment 'modules are not recursive' states a rule only the ModuleExp path enforces. Decide which behavior is intended before pinning it.

The info for nodes inside a module definition now comes from the Let's pass, not the direct pass. Two editor-visible differences follow: ancestors gain a duplicated module id, matching the body (AutoProbePerform.re:77-93 already dedups this); and inside a function-valued module that does not name itself, the recorded ctx includes the module's own name, so completions or the inspector may offer F there. Neither changes elaboration. With a livelit inside the definition, the livelit's add_missing_info (Statics.re:1656-1657) no longer mixes infos from two passes.

Pass counts in the title: on today's dev, the Let's recursion probe (Statics.re:2070) runs for every let. So a plain module definition goes from 3 analyses to 2, not from 2 to 1. 'Once, not twice' is exact for the ModuleExp case's own extra pass, and for the whole binding only once #2603 lands. Self-naming modules still pay the full count (5 on dev and on the PR).

Test strength: test_module_names_itself uses inconsistent_typecheck, which passes if any static error exists anywhere (Test_Statics_Prelude.re:225-242). The PR description's evidence (`hazel analyze -W` byte-identical on 73 programs; modules.hz prints 6 Measured 'id not found' warnings before, 4 after) compares diagnostics, not the info map or elaborations. notes.summary:
What the code does. Hazel type-checks `module M = def in body` by turning it into `let M = def in body`. The new let keeps the module binding's own id (Statics.re:2736-2742 at origin/dev). Once the let is analyzed, the ModuleExp case on dev analyzes `def` a second time, on its own (Statics.re:2757-2762). That second pass exists only to get `def`'s elaboration without the let's wrapping. The let's elaboration wraps `def` in a label alignment and a name (2184-2187), or in a fixpoint when the definition refers to itself (2189-2229). `ModuleHelpers.moduleexp_elab` puts the bare elaboration back in the let and strips the signature ascription from the pattern (ModuleHelpers.re:448-456). #2651 ("a module binding analyzes its definition once, not twice") skips that second pass. `add` records each node's info at the node's ids, and the info's `elab_term` is the very value `add` returns (Statics.re:249-268). So after the let's analysis, the info stored at `rep_id(def)` already holds the elaboration the second pass would rebuild. The PR reads it back with one `Id.Map.find_opt`, a balanced-tree lookup (29c08fd8fa Statics.re:2775-2780). It falls back to the old second pass when the let produced a fixpoint (`names_itself`, 2770-2774) or when no info was recorded (2781-2788). The architectural change is that the statics map, not a second traversal, now carries `def`'s elaboration to the ModuleExp case. Also, `def`'s subtree in the map is now last written by the let's pass. On dev the second pass overwrote it.

How much work it removes. The let on dev always runs a recursion probe over `def` and throws its map away (Statics.re:2070), then the real pass (2079). A module literal is never function-shaped (Exp.re:456), so it takes this non-recursive path. With the second pass, every module binding on dev costs 3 analyses of `def`. #2651 alone brings that to 2, and #2603 ("a let is analyzed once unless it refers to itself") alone also brings it to 2. Together they bring it to 1. The PR's word "twice" is true where #2603 is already in place, as on the livelits branches the measurements came from. The multipliers stack with nesting, but only some nesting goes through this code. A nested module written as an item inside braces (`module Inner = {...}`, no `in`) is a ModuleMod, which is lowered to a plain let (ModuleHelpers.re:300-304) and never reaches the ModuleExp case. That kind costs ×2 per level on dev because of the let's probe, which is #2603's fix, not this PR's. #2651's doubling compounds as 2^depth (3^depth on dev with the probe) only when a `module … in` expression sits inside another module binding's definition. No corpus program does that: dev's only module program, `docs/reference/modules.hz`, nests only by items. A third multiplier also applies to module bindings. An expression checked against a one-field labeled product is analyzed once without a type first (Statics.re:2778-2789), and the auto-label path then analyzes it twice more (313, 337). By my reading, a module under a one-member signature that has an extra member is analyzed 4 times per pass. That gives modules.hz:165-168 3×4×2 = 24 analyses of its member `1` on dev, which matches the 24 that #2689 reports for modules.hz. After #2603 and #2651 it is 1×4×1 = 4.

Measurements. On dev the effect is small and inside the noise. On a made-up module of 800 functions, statics is about 0.13 s of 6 s, and whole-command times overlap (6.06 and 6.74 s before, 5.26 and 6.05 s after, two runs each). Most of that time goes to `MakeTerm.from_zip_for_sem`, a separate lead. The real payoff showed on the livelits branch (#2635). There a profile of *Shirt and Pants* put 1.79 s of 4.2 s of statics in the second pass, against 2.06 s in the let's pass. CLI statics went from 6.7 to 4.3 s, against 4.1 s for the same slide with the module flattened into top-level lets, so the fix removes the module's whole overhead. *Shoes and Hair* went from 8.8 to 5.8 s. These were two runs each, within 0.3 s of each other. There is no browser number for this fix on its own.

Where it sits. #2651 is the smallest open performance PR against dev (+55/−5, 3 files, CI green at 29c08fd8fa). It touches only the ModuleExp case and merges cleanly with #2603: #2689's merge of the two, ea45d5342a, has no conflict hunks. #2689 (draft: "statics analyzes each expression within a budget") is the CI guard for both fixes, but it merged #2651 at e3013b0360, without the self-naming fallback. #2597 and #2635 also carry only e3013b0360's version. Alexander's open Modules II stack (#2493 to #2510) keeps the second pass, with `~coercible=true` from part 2 on. Whichever lands second needs a one-line merge in the fallback, as the livelits branch already has. Its gain on dev grows as module programs arrive: module bindings appear in 1 corpus file on dev, 4 at the top of Modules II and 13 on the livelits branch.

facts.claim: ModuleExp is checked by building `Let(pat, def, body)` that carries the ModuleExp's own rep id (IdTagged.fast_copy) and analyzing it with the same ana.

On dev, after the let's analysis, `def` is analyzed again directly, against the Asc pattern's type or syn, and the resulting map is threaded on, so this pass is the last to write infos for def's subtree.

The second pass is used only to supply `def_elab_direct`, which moduleexp_elab puts in place of the let's definition, with the signature ascription stripped from the pattern; a non-Let expanded elab ignores it.

What the let wraps around def's elaboration: align_exp_if_needed plus add_name in the ordinary case, or a FixF with a fresh-deterministic inner id when the definition is recursive and refers to its binder.
`add` builds the Info.exp with `elab_term` set to the elab it returns, and records it at IdTagged.ids(user_term). This is the invariant the read-back relies on.
The statics map is Id.Map.t(Info.t), an OCaml Map over UUIDs (balanced tree, O(log n) lookup). add_info is last-writer-wins via Id.Map.add.
The PR reads def's elaboration back from the InfoExp at Exp.rep_id(def) unless the let's elaboration is `Let(_, FixF(_), _)`. Otherwise it falls back to the old direct pass.
On dev the Let case always runs a recursion probe over def and discards its map, then the real pass (non-recursive). The recursive path runs probe + three passes (2091, 2103, 2121).

A module literal is never function-shaped: get_num_of_functions returns None for Module and ModuleExp. So a module binding's let takes the non-recursive path: probe + real = 2 analyses on dev, plus the direct pass = 3.
#2603's let-once commit makes the probe lazy and skips it for non-function-shaped definitions, so a module literal gets one let pass. It does not touch the ModuleExp case.

Against a one-field labeled product, an expression is first analyzed in synthesis mode, then again by default_case, or by autolabel_singleton_tuple, which analyzes a fresh copy (313) and the wrapped tuple (336-343, itself pre-passed). By my reading that is 4 analyses in the autolabel case.

autolabel_singleton_tuple returns `(l = original_expression)`, where original_expression is an unelaborated fresh copy of the source, but it records the copy's own analysis (inner_for_source) at the def's ids. review_points: On dev alone the change is 3 analyses of def to 2, not 2 to 1. The let's discarded probe (Statics.re:2070) is the other extra pass, and #2603 removes it. The description's 'twice what it should' is true only with #2603. Say so, or merge them as a pair.

The 2^depth story applies to a `module … in` inside another module binding's definition. Item-form nesting (`module Inner = {...}` inside braces) never reaches the ModuleExp case (ModuleHelpers.re:300-304). Its per-level x2 on dev is the let probe, which is #2603's fix. No corpus program nests the expression form, so #2651's measured win is a constant factor per binding: large when one module holds most of a program (livelits), small on dev.

Evidence quality: the dev timing overlaps (two runs each), and the PR says so. The headline numbers (1.79 s of 4.2 s; 6.7 to 4.3 s) come from #2635, which carries #2603 and per-item statics. There is no browser measurement of this fix alone. The flattened-module baseline (4.1 s) is the strongest argument that the fix removes the whole module overhead.

The read-back rests on 'add records the elab_term it returns' (Statics.re:249-268). Check the known exceptions: (a) the FixF case, handled by names_itself; (b) autolabel_singleton_tuple records a different info than it returns (Statics.re:356-357). That is the one-member-signature corner, whose new behaviour is kept and pinned; (c) a Tuple def is rearranged by the let before analysis (Statics.re:2054-2069), so the read-back elab is the rearranged one where dev's direct pass was not. Is that reachable for a module binding?

Under #2603's probe reuse, a function-valued module definition (`module F = fun x -> …`) is recorded from the probe, which ran with F in scope (p_syn.ctx). Before #2651, the direct pass overwrote those infos. Together, completion and hover inside the definition may see F at its synthesized type. The elaboration is unaffected. Worth one check with both merged.
